name: velaris
description: Write Velaris, see what it can touch, and run it in a box.
long_description:
Velaris is a language where a function's signature declares its types, the effects it may perform, whether it can fail, and promises a theorem prover checks before the program runs.

This connector gives four tools: read the language card (about 2,300 words, enough to write correct Velaris), check a program without running it, audit what it can touch and how much of its promises are proven, and run it under an effect budget you choose. A program run with allow: ["io"] cannot read files, reach the network or call Python, whatever its source claims - and a refusal cannot be caught by the program.

Not a security boundary: allowing ffi grants everything Python can do.

tools.name: velaris_card
tools.description: The Velaris language, small enough to read before writing it.

tools.name: velaris_check
tools.description: Compile without running; problems with codes, lines and fixes.

tools.name: velaris_audit
tools.description: What a program touches, promises, and can fail at.

tools.name: velaris_run
tools.description: Run under an effect budget; anything outside it is refused.
